description: M12 phase F: closed-loop following with the head camera rendered in the loop (bipe.m12.rendered_link)
status: Phase F plan approved (22 October 2026); 5 ms exposure with the phase C tracker chosen by the user (22 October 2026, 18:45 UTC); 74 deg view gate and side-light losses accepted for phase E, signed off by the user (24 October 2026)
output_dir_basis: The 5 ms matrix; the 10 ms runs (retry_and_grow seed-0 check and nominal seeds) stay in artifacts/m12/following_rendered and the 10 ms phase_c check in artifacts/m12/following_rendered_phase_c
exposure_basis: User decision (22 October 2026): 5 ms instead of the phase C 10 ms. The phase F check found the rendered misses follow the body pitch rate (vertical motion blur from the balance core's ~10 Hz oscillation: under 20 deg/s 0 % missed, 60-100 deg/s 51 %), which the phase C and D models did not include; at 5 ms, straight_0.6, approach and corner_90 (seed 0) detected 1589 of 1590 possible frames with no losses. The noise budget follows the exposure (half the light per frame); the dim variant tests 50 lx at 5 ms
pose_conversion_basis: As phase C: the tag pose is turned into range and bearing with the plant's own camera pose (lean and pitch included), as if the Pi knew it. 'fixed_mount' (the camera of the robot standing level at the nominal posture) is the diagnostic for a Pi that is not told the lean

phase_c.basis: The phase C pipeline: after a region-of-interest miss the next frame is a full-frame search; the window is the last detection's box x2 plus 24 px

retry_and_grow.basis: Proposed after the phase F check (22 October 2026): about 4 % of ordinary frames cannot be decoded with the tag well inside the window (single-frame image misses), so one region miss is retried on the next frame before a full search; and the window's margin grows with the detection's age at 1.5 rad/s (the 1.0 rad/s yaw envelope plus the target's crossing rate), so the window after a full search (about 0.27 s old) still covers the tag in turns. A larger window costs more detector time on the Pi; the phase C timing is not rescaled (an estimate gap). Not chosen: the user picked 5 ms with the phase C tracker (22 October 2026)

view_gate_basis: User decision (24 October 2026): the Pi drops a tag pose whose fitted 3-D view angle (tag normal against the line of sight) is past 74 deg, about 69-70 deg of yaw view angle, and sends the frame as an empty report (detected false, which the follower counts as BIPE_FOLLOW_EMPTY); the tracker keeps the tag. The gate is bipe.pi.gate, the Pi's code, which the simulator runs. Past 70 deg of yaw the fitted range reads 1.4-2.0 cm short (+1.3 cm below 30 deg), and the last such reading before the corner_90 miss made the coast predict the person approaching and the robot reverse. A 65 deg gate dropped good frames and the coast ran out. Only the 12 matrix runs with a detection past 60 deg of yaw view angle are rerun with the gate; the others have no frame it can act on

nominal.basis: The phase C scene as rendered: the M10 plant's spot light (bipe.m10.plant) and the M12 directional light (bipe.m12.scenarios.world_xml), with the 200 lx noise budget (config/perception-m12.json camera.noise)

dim.basis: The phase C dim comparison, 50 lx (camera.noise.low_light_lux). Auto exposure and gain bring white to the same level under the 10 ms exposure cap, so dim light shows as sensor noise, not a darker image

side_light.basis: Assumption: a strong low light from one side (a window), about 20 degrees above the horizon, with the spot and headlight turned down to little fill; the tag face is lit unevenly and the floor brightly. Matte paper and ink, no specular glare (the phase C materials)

basis: User decisions (22 October 2026, phase F plan approved as recommended): run phase F before phase E with the phase C camera pose and timing estimate; latency drawn from the phase C Pi Zero 2 W estimate by tracker mode; 5 nominal seeds (the renders are deterministic, so seeds vary only latency and sensor noise); dim and strong side light on three scenarios
lights_order: The scene's lights in model order: the M10 plant's spot light, then the M12 directional light
